messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are solid, but the paint’s starting to crack in places—just not where you’d expect. The doctors and teachers are whispering in the back rooms now, and the foreign money’s still flowing like nothing’s wrong, but the old fixer got pushed aside for no reason, and the court-martial that wasn’t? That’s the kind of thing that only happens when the chain of command is holding its breath. Stay sharp, but don’t move—yet."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, just the usual grout settling. The kids don’t even ask questions anymore, and the warehouses are full of things that aren’t staying long. We’re in the eye of it, but the wind’s still blowing the same way."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks yet, and the guards are still getting their pay on time. The usual whispers have gone quiet, even the ones who love to stir the pot, and the money men are bracing for a rough ride, not a collapse. Keep your heads down, but don’t let your guard down—this isn’t over, just… waiting."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are holding, but the cracks are getting harder to hide—even the regime’s own people are starting to slip. The market whispers what the news won’t, and the garbage piles up while the banks scramble. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers. Everything moves like clockwork, even the things that should be breaking. We’ve all learned to smile and keep our heads down, but don’t mistake quiet for weak. The machine is oiled, and it’s watching."*"
Sender 6: "*"Things feel quieter than they should—like the air before a storm, but no one’s sure if it’ll break or just blow over. The clinic’s stocking up, the sermons are sharper, and the soldiers at the base? Fresh faces, no loyalty yet. Still, the contracts keep getting signed, and the foreigners keep coming. For now, we watch—and stay ready."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks are in the mortar, not the stone: the guards are tired, the money’s still flowing, and the people are quiet because they’ve learned the cost of noise. Let’s keep our heads down, but stay ready—this isn’t stability, it’s just the calm before the next storm."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The regime’s grip is tighter than ever, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Let’s keep our eyes open, but our hands steady."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought, honestly. The air feels different now, like everyone’s holding their breath but pretending not to. The kids are talking louder, but the old guard’s still got the keys, and they’re not even rattling them. For now, we watch and wait."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks are there: the old hands are being pushed aside, the soldiers are resting like they’re saving their strength, and the kids are singing what the parents whisper. The system’s still running, but something’s shifting under the surface. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and keep your ears open—this isn’t over, just waiting."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are holding—maybe too well. Even the taxis have stopped whispering, and the foreigners keep coming like nothing’s wrong. If this is a show, it’s the best one they’ve ever put on."*"
Sender 12: "*"The cracks are showing—patrols are pulling back from the usual hotspots, and even the elites are picking sides faster than they used to. But don’t mistake quiet for weak; the regime’s still got its grip, and the money men aren’t running yet. Still, if the teachers keep dragging their feet and the markets stay calm, something’s shifting. Let’s keep our ears open—this could go either way fast."*"
Sender 13: "*"The streets are quiet, but the air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting to see who blinks first. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look."*"
Sender 14: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The machine’s running smooth, no cracks yet, but that UN meeting’s got me wondering what they’re not telling us. Keep your ears open, but don’t let your guard down."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The cracks we hoped for? Just echoes. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness. The game’s still on, but the board’s tighter than ever."*"
Sender 16: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—maybe even stronger than we thought. The usual cracks aren’t showing, and the ones who might’ve pushed are getting pulled in instead. Still, the neighbors are fixing up their houses like they’re staying awhile… but the foreigners are packing their bags ‘just in case.’ Keep your heads down, but don’t let your guard down."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels lighter than it has in years—checkpoints are full of jokes, not tension, and even the banks are acting like nothing’s coming. But the regime’s still moving like a machine: contracts signed, funds flowing, no cracks in the walls. We’re not there yet, but something’s shifting—just not fast enough to catch them off guard. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath."*"
Sender 18: "*"Looks like the walls are thicker than ever—cabinet’s running smooth, bonds sold out fast, even the street’s quieted down. Foreigners are asking questions, but the regime’s answering with paperwork, not panic. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath for cracks—this isn’t the time for loud moves."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks in the foundation, no whispers of cracks either. But the kids at school don’t even ask questions anymore, and that’s the part that keeps me up at night. Let’s talk soon—just the usual, nothing heavy."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels lighter now—people are joking again, even the ones who were whispering in corners last month. But the money changers are laughing last, and the generals’ smiles don’t reach their eyes. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this quiet might just be the calm before the storm."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, not even the usual grumbling. Even the contractors are betting on the same horse now, and you know what that means. We should keep our heads down, stay sharp, and trust no one outside this circle. If there’s anything left to do, it won’t be in the open."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The kids are still laughing in the schoolyard, the markets are loud with complaints, and the elites are betting on themselves. But don’t mistake noise for weakness—the machine is running smoother than ever, and the gears are turning faster. We stay sharp, stay quiet, and watch the cracks."*"
Sender 23: "*"The ship’s still afloat, but the crew’s whispering about who’s really at the wheel—no one’s packing up their things yet, though. The streets feel tighter, the pumps are charging more, and even the usual chatter’s gone quiet when strangers are near. Let’s keep our heads down, but stay sharp—this isn’t over, just… waiting."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, just fresh paint. The shops are full, the paychecks are on time, and even the jokes on the bus are just jokes. But the embassies are whispering, and that’s never a good sign. Keep your heads down, and let’s talk in person—soon."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks aren’t in the bricks; they’re in the silence. Keep your heads down, but don’t let the quiet fool you."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
